stages.summary: North Korean forces crossed the 38th parallel on 25 June 1950.
stages.title: 전쟁 발발

stages.summary: A broad early-war southward advance preceded the southeastern defensive perimeter; no daily front coordinates are supplied.
stages.title: 북한군 남하

stages.summary: Republic of Korea and UN forces defended the southeastern Busan/Nakdong perimeter. The existing September 1 shape is schematic.
stages.title: 낙동강 방어선

stages.summary: The Incheon amphibious landing occurred on 15 September 1950; no landing-route or occupation geometry is supplied.
stages.title: 인천상륙작전

stages.summary: Seoul was recaptured in the September counteroffensive; September 28 is the conventional recapture date, not a certificate of city-block control.
stages.title: 서울 수복

presentationPolicy.contextNote: The northward advance continued beyond this editorial window toward November24. The retained map is the earlier September1 schematic snapshot, explicitly dated, not the actual front on these chapter days.

stages.summary: Republic of Korea and UN forces advanced north during the autumn. This overlaps the first Chinese combat in October; the existing November 24 snapshot is later than that entry.
stages.title: 국군·유엔군 북진

presentationPolicy.contextNote: October25 first Chinese combat is explained separately from the held September1 map. Do not use the later November24 northern snapshot as the October25 front.

stages.summary: The preserved participation policy uses October 25 for first Chinese ground combat, distinct from October 19 border crossing and the major late-November counteroffensive.
stages.title: 중국군 참전

presentationPolicy.contextNote: Start from the explicitly dated November24 supplied northern snapshot, then use the supplied January4 withdrawal snapshot. Their crossfade is a schematic visual transition, not a daily reconstructed line.

stages.summary: Chinese and North Korean offensives drove the front south; the existing January 4 snapshot represents Seoul withdrawal approximately.
stages.title: 전선 남하

stages.summary: Republic of Korea and UN forces recovered ground in 1951. No additional exact front or unit movement is persisted.
stages.title: 국군·유엔군 재반격

stages.summary: A broad stalemate developed near the 38th parallel; a label does not supply an exact initial stalemate date or control polygon.
stages.title: 38선 부근 교착

stages.summary: Fighting and local front changes continued before armistice. No persisted 1951–1953 local front-change track is available.
stages.title: 1951~1953 전선 변화

stages.summary: The armistice was signed on 27 July 1953. Existing final geometry is an approximate simplified present border, not the surveyed 1953 MDL.
stages.title: 1953 정전협정

narration.summary: North Korean forces crossed the 38th parallel on 25 June 1950.
A broad early-war southward advance preceded the southeastern defensive perimeter; no daily front coordinates are supplied.
Republic of Korea and UN forces defended the southeastern Busan/Nakdong perimeter. The existing September 1 shape is schematic.
The Incheon amphibious landing occurred on 15 September 1950; no landing-route or occupation geometry is supplied.
Seoul was recaptured in the September counteroffensive; September 28 is the conventional recapture date, not a certificate of city-block control.
Republic of Korea and UN forces advanced north during the autumn. This overlaps the first Chinese combat in October; the existing November 24 snapshot is later than that entry.

presentationPolicy.contextNote: The northward advance continued beyond this editorial window toward November24. The retained map is the earlier September1 schematic snapshot, explicitly dated, not the actual front on these chapter days.

narration.summary: The preserved participation policy uses October 25 for first Chinese ground combat, distinct from October 19 border crossing and the major late-November counteroffensive.

presentationPolicy.contextNote: October25 first Chinese combat is explained separately from the held September1 map. Do not use the later November24 northern snapshot as the October25 front.

narration.summary: Chinese and North Korean offensives drove the front south; the existing January 4 snapshot represents Seoul withdrawal approximately.

presentationPolicy.contextNote: Start from the explicitly dated November24 supplied northern snapshot, then use the supplied January4 withdrawal snapshot. Their crossfade is a schematic visual transition, not a daily reconstructed line.

narration.summary: Republic of Korea and UN forces recovered ground in 1951. No additional exact front or unit movement is persisted.
A broad stalemate developed near the 38th parallel; a label does not supply an exact initial stalemate date or control polygon.
Fighting and local front changes continued before armistice. No persisted 1951–1953 local front-change track is available.
The armistice was signed on 27 July 1953. Existing final geometry is an approximate simplified present border, not the surveyed 1953 MDL.
